hypothesis.title: Minimum Viable Gesture
hypothesis.question: What is the smallest local musical unit that can still carry recognizable compositional identity under layer removal, filtering, or cropping?
hypothesis.hypothesis: If a local gesture couples a nearest-neighbor harmonic graph move, a recurring voicing unit, a call-response behavior, and a subtle spectral trace, then it will remain more recognizable under damage than a gesture whose identity is concentrated in one foreground motif.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: The APC source shows that identity can be distributed across phase/log-magnitude relationships and survive compression, resampling, and 20% end-cropping [S3]. The HHL source constrains coherent melody-harmony selection to 2-note / 2-chord blocks, implying that small coupled blocks can carry musically meaningful structure [S5]. The basso continuo source reports player identification from griffs, suggesting local voicing units can encode personal style [S6]. Tonnetz geometry supplies graph adjacency for defining nearest harmonic moves [S2], while the ice source motivates nearest-accessible path dependence rather than global optimization [S1]. Mayer's call-response practice adds a practical arrangement layer for paired local gestures [S4].

recipe.title: Gesture Survival Test
recipe.bodyMd: Build a one-minute piece from eight one- or two-bar gestures. Each gesture couples one nearest-neighbor graph move [S2], one griff-like voicing unit [S6], one call-response answer by silence, register, timbre, percussion, or melody [S4], and one subtle spectral trace inspired by APC's hidden frequency-domain channel [S3]. Borrow the ice-source rule that each transition should move to the nearest accessible state rather than the globally most resolved destination [S1]. Keep melody and harmony chosen as a coupled block before rendering, echoing the HHL source's small coherent blocks [S5]. Render the full mix, a lead-muted version, an 8 kHz low-pass version, and a final-20%-cropped version. Score whether identity survives each damage condition.

parameters.value: nearest-neighbor graph move plus call-response answer

dawChecklist: Create an eight-node harmonic graph and mark allowed nearest-neighbor moves.
Design four griff-like voicing units and assign one to each gesture.
For every call, choose one response behavior: silence, lower register, darker timbre, percussion fill, or melodic answer.
Bind a subtle EQ, phase, or noise-color trace to each griff.
Render full mix, lead-muted mix, 8 kHz low-pass mix, and final-20%-cropped mix.
Rate each render from 1 to 5 for whether the same compositional identity survives.

protocol.listeningContext: Level-matched DAW bounces over the same monitors or headphones.
protocol.listeningMethod: Blind or shuffled comparison of full and damaged renders.
whatVaries: identity concentrated in lead vs distributed across gesture layers
